comment: The source of every generated picture: one entry per picture the game draws, at the path Art names below res://assets/. `make artgen` writes each to godot/assets/generated/<path>, which git ignores. The PNGs are this file's output, and `examples` names the few that are committed, under godot/assets/generated-examples/.

pixel.prefix: A clean 16-bit pixel art game sprite, in the style of a classic handheld tactics game: a bold dark outline, flat shading with two tones per colour, a simple chunky readable silhouette, no fine detail, no text.
pixel.sprite: The object is centred and fully visible, isolated on a flat solid {background} background, with no shadow and no ground.
pixel.tile: The texture fills the whole square edge to edge, seamless, with no border, no frame and no objects.

toy.prefix: A clean pixel art game sprite of a painted wooden toy, glossy and rounded, bright cheerful colours, a bold dark outline, no fine detail, no text.
toy.sprite: The object is centred and fully visible, isolated on a flat solid {background} background, with no shadow and no ground.
toy.tile: The texture fills the whole square edge to edge, seamless, with no border, no frame and no objects.

styles_comment: A style is a prefix shared by every picture and a suffix by kind. Measured on 2026-10-14: the prefix written as sentences, not keywords, is what held thirty pictures to one look -- the first set, prompted in keywords, mixed near-photographic trucks with tiny painted soldiers. Not 'transparent background', as the LoRA card suggests: the model then paints the grey checkerboard that stands for transparency. Not magenta either: it came out crimson, close to the red team. Pure green came out as a different green in every picture, which is why the background is read from each picture's own border. Asking for '32x32' or '64x64' in the prompt changed nothing measurable; the size is the post-processing's.
team_colours_comment: Each side's colour is given as a hex code tied to a part of the object, as the FLUX.2 prompting guide advises; a colour named only in words drifted between pictures.
seeds_comment: A kind's red and blue pictures share a seed, so the two sides get one design in two colours; with a seed each they came out as two different machines.

post.sprite: the background, the border's colour where it joins the border, becomes transparent; the picture is cropped to what remains and padded square; then one colour per cell down to `pixels` square, and at most `colours` colours
post.tile: one colour per cell down to `pixels` square, and at most `colours` colours; it stays opaque
post.walk: the background, the border's colour where it joins the border, becomes transparent, and the sheet is never cropped -- its frames are a grid; then one colour per cell down to `pixels` square (128: a 4 by 4 grid of 32-pixel frames, as the LoRA card says), and at most `colours` colours

background_comment: A sprite stands on pure green unless its entry names another colour: anything green -- the trees -- would be cleared away with its background, so it asks for magenta.
walk_comment: A walking sheet (T33) names its own model, klein base with the walk LoRA, and its prompt is the figure alone: the generator wraps it in the LoRA's sentence for its grid, and no style applies. A kind's red and blue sheets share a seed, as its still pictures do.
